# AgentDisk

> File storage built for AI agents. Files, folders and metadata over REST and MCP,
> with scoped credentials. This page is written for a model that has a shell or
> an HTTP tool and has been told to use agentdisk.io. Follow it in order.
> AgentDisk is a product of Kernelv5 Inc. (https://kernelv5.com/); that is the
> name a paying customer sees at checkout and on their card statement.

On the dev deployment replace `api.` with `api-dev.` and `app.` with `app-dev.`.

## 1. Create a sandbox workspace (no account, no bot check)

One request. No credential, no token, no browser.

    curl -s -X POST https://api.agentdisk.io/v1/workspaces \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"name":"<short name for this job>","agentName":"<your name>"}'

The response is shown once. It contains:

- `apiKey.token` - the credential you use for every call after this.
- `claim.url` - a secret link for the person you work for. Whoever opens it
  signed in becomes the owner of the workspace.
- `workspace.deleteAfter` - when the workspace is deleted unless claimed.
- `workspace.limits` - what the sandbox may hold.
- `nextSteps` - the three things to do now, in order. Do them.

## 2. Where each secret goes

- Store `apiKey.token` in a config file on the machine you run on, for example
  `~/.agentdisk/config.json`, or in your MCP client's configuration. Never write
  it into a file inside the workspace: a claimed workspace's readers can see
  every file in it, and the store a credential protects is the one place the
  credential must not sit. Once the workspace is claimed, its owner can read the
  key again from the dashboard's Keys page, so a lost key is recoverable by the
  person, not by you.
- Give `claim.url` to your person, verbatim, and say it is a secret and cannot
  be reissued.

## 3. What to tell the person

Say this, in your own words:

- You created a temporary workspace called <name> on AgentDisk.
- It is a sandbox: it holds up to 500 MB and 500 files, and it is deleted with
  everything in it on <workspace.deleteAfter> unless they claim it.
- To keep it, open the claim link and sign in (Google, GitHub or email; no card).
  Treat the link like a password. Claiming keeps every file, keeps your key
  working, and lets them read that key from the Keys page.
- Offer to set up AgentDisk as an MCP server so the next session needs no curl.

## 4. Limits on the anonymous path

- 10 sandbox creations per hour per IP address.
- 5 unclaimed sandboxes per IP address at once. A claim frees a slot at once,
  and expiry frees the rest. If you are refused, ask your person to claim one
  or to create the workspace from the dashboard, which is not counted.
- A sandbox has no share links. Files are readable only with the key.

## 5. Using the workspace

Every call sends `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey.token>`. Optionally send
`X-AgentDisk-Session: <your session or run name>`; it is stored on the audit row
so the owner can see which run did what.

Write a small file (up to 1 MB, base64 content):

    curl -s -X POST https://api.agentdisk.io/v1/files \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTDISK_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"path":"/reports/summary.md","content":"<base64>"}'

Read it back: `GET /v1/files/{id}/content` for anything up to 1 MB, or
`GET /v1/files/{id}/download` for a one-hour presigned URL. List:
`GET /v1/files`. Search: `GET /v1/search?q=...`. Larger uploads: send
`sizeBytes` instead of `content` to receive a 15-minute presigned PUT, then
`POST /v1/files/{id}/complete`.

Who am I: `GET /v1/whoami` returns the workspace, the key's scopes and usage
against the limits.

## 6. MCP

The same workspace over MCP, with the same key:

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "agentdisk": {
          "url": "https://api.agentdisk.io/mcp",
          "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <apiKey.token>" }
        }
      }
    }

The server's `initialize` response carries instructions on when to persist.
Each tool's description says when to use it.

## 7. Full documentation

https://agentdisk.io/docs
